claim: AWS DataSync is an online data movement service that simplifies and accelerates data migrations to AWS and moving data to and from on-premises storage, other cloud providers, and AWS storage services.
question: What is AWS DataSync?

values.display: online data movement service

evidence.quote: AWS DataSync is an online data movement service that simplifies and accelerates data migrations to AWS as well as moving data to and from on-premises storage, other cloud providers, and AWS Storage services.

claim: AWS DataSync supports moving data to, from, or between Amazon S3, Amazon EFS, Amazon FSx for Windows File Server, Amazon FSx for Lustre, Amazon FSx for OpenZFS and Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP.
question: Which AWS Storage services are supported by AWS DataSync?

values.display: Amazon S3, Amazon EFS, Amazon FSx

evidence.quote: AWS DataSync supports moving data to, from, or between Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3), Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS), Amazon FSx for Windows File Server, Amazon FSx for Lustre, Amazon FSx for OpenZFS, and Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP.

claim: To migrate with DataSync you configure it to make an initial copy of the whole dataset and then schedule incremental transfers of changing data until the final cut-over from on premises to AWS.
question: How do I use AWS DataSync to migrate data to AWS?

values.display: initial copy of your entire dataset

evidence.quote: Configure DataSync to make an initial copy of your entire dataset, and schedule subsequent incremental transfers of changing data until the final cut-over from on-premises to AWS.

claim: DataSync is ideal for customers who need online migrations for active data sets, timely transfers for continuously generated data, or replication for business continuity.
question: When is AWS DataSync the right choice?

values.display: online migrations for active data sets

evidence.quote: DataSync is ideal for customers who need online migrations for active data sets, timely transfers for continuously generated data, or replication for business continuity.

claim: DataSync can copy data from Google Cloud Storage using the Amazon S3 API, from Azure Files using the SMB protocol, and from Azure Blob Storage including Azure Data Lake Storage Gen 2.
question: Can I use AWS DataSync to copy data from other clouds to AWS?

values.display: Google Cloud Storage using the Amazon S3 API

qualifiers.scope: AWS DataSync, other clouds to AWS

evidence.quote: Yes. Using AWS DataSync, you can copy data from Google Cloud Storage using the Amazon S3 API, from Azure Files using the SMB protocol, or from Azure Blob Storage (including Azure Data Lake Storage Gen 2).

claim: With Enhanced mode tasks no agent is needed to connect to other cloud storage; with Basic mode you deploy the DataSync agent in your cloud environment or on Amazon EC2.
question: Do I need a DataSync agent to copy data from another cloud?

values.display: no agent is required to connect to your cloud storage

qualifiers.scope: AWS DataSync, transfers from other clouds
qualifiers.condition: Enhanced mode needs no agent; Basic mode needs an agent

evidence.quote: When using Enhanced mode tasks, no agent is required to connect to your cloud storage. Otherwise, if using Basic mode, deploy the DataSync agent in your cloud environment or on Amazon EC2.

claim: DataSync has two agent types that match the task modes, Basic and Enhanced; you need the Enhanced mode agent to copy between an on-premises NFS or SMB file server and S3 in Enhanced mode, and the Basic mode agent for all other use cases.
question: How do I deploy an AWS DataSync agent?

values.display: two types of agents that correspond to different task modes

qualifiers.condition: Enhanced mode agent only for on-premises NFS or SMB to S3 in Enhanced mode

evidence.quote: AWS DataSync supports two types of agents that correspond to different task modes: Basic and Enhanced. When copying data between your on-premises NFS or SMB file server and Amazon S3 using Enhanced mode, you need to use the DataSync Enhanced mode agent. For all other use cases, use the DataSync Basic mode agent.

note: The current user guide (choosing-task-mode) says Enhanced mode agents also serve HDFS and other sources; later Enhanced mode locations (2026-07-28) are not examinable yet.

claim: To copy data to or from on-premises storage, you download the DataSync agent virtual machine image from the AWS console and deploy it on VMware ESXi, Linux KVM, Nutanix AHV (using the KVM agent image) or Microsoft Hyper-V.
question: Which hypervisors can run the DataSync agent on premises?

values.display: VMware ESXi, Linux Kernel-based Virtual Machine (KVM), Nutanix AHV

evidence.quote: To copy data to or from your on-premises storage, you download the agent virtual machine image from the AWS Console and deploy to your on-premises VMware ESXi, Linux Kernel-based Virtual Machine (KVM), Nutanix AHV (using the KVM agent image), or Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

claim: Deploying a DataSync agent is not required to transfer data between AWS storage services within the same AWS account.
question: Do I need a DataSync agent to copy between AWS storage services?

values.display: Deploying an agent is not required

qualifiers.scope: AWS DataSync, AWS storage services in one account

evidence.quote: Deploying an agent is not required to transfer data between AWS Storage services within the same AWS account. To copy data to or from a self-managed in-cloud file server, or between AWS Storage services in different AWS accounts, you launch an Amazon EC2 instance using a DataSync agent AMI.

claim: A Basic mode task is subject to quotas on the number of files and objects in a dataset, and it prepares, transfers and verifies sequentially, so it is slower than Enhanced mode for most workloads.
question: What is the difference between Basic mode and Enhanced mode tasks?

values.display: subject to quotas on the number of files and objects

evidence.quote: A Basic mode task is subject to quotas on the number of files and objects in a dataset. Basic mode sequentially prepares, transfers, and verifies files and objects in a dataset, making it slower than Enhanced mode for most workloads.

claim: With Enhanced mode you can transfer datasets with virtually unlimited numbers of objects at higher performance than Basic mode, because it lists, prepares, transfers and verifies data in parallel.
question: What does Enhanced mode do better than Basic mode?

values.display: virtually unlimited numbers of objects

evidence.quote: With Enhanced mode, you can transfer datasets with virtually unlimited numbers of objects at higher levels of performance than Basic mode. Enhanced mode tasks optimize and streamline the data transfer process by listing, preparing, transferring, and verifying data in parallel.

claim: The DataSync FAQ says Enhanced mode is currently available for transfers between S3 locations, between other clouds and S3, and between on-premises NFS or SMB file servers and S3, and that Basic mode supports all DataSync location types.
question: Where is DataSync Enhanced mode available?

values.display: between Amazon S3 locations, between other clouds and Amazon S3

qualifiers.scope: AWS DataSync Enhanced mode, as stated in the FAQ
qualifiers.condition: Basic mode supports all location types

evidence.quote: Enhanced mode is currently available for transfers between Amazon S3 locations, between other clouds and Amazon S3, and between on-premises NFS or SMB file servers and Amazon S3. Basic mode supports all DataSync location types available today.

note: The user guide page choosing-task-mode lists more Enhanced mode locations (EFS, FSx for Lustre, FSx for OpenZFS, HDFS, Azure Blob); Enhanced mode for those was announced on 2026-07-28 and is not examinable yet. The FAQ conflicts with the guide here.

claim: While transferring and storing data, DataSync checks that the data written to the destination matches the data read from the source, and an optional verification check can compare source and destination at the end of the transfer.
question: How does AWS DataSync ensure my data is copied correctly?

values.display: optional verification check

evidence.quote: As AWS DataSync transfers and stores data, it performs integrity checks to ensure the data written to the destination matches the data read from the source. Additionally, an optional verification check can be performed to compare source and destination at the end of the transfer.

claim: In DataSync, filters and manifests cannot be used together.
question: Can I use filters and a manifest in the same DataSync task?

values.display: filters and manifests cannot be used together

evidence.quote: Note that filters and manifests cannot be used together.

claim: A DataSync manifest is a CSV-formatted file that lists the file paths or object keys to include in a task run, which limits what DataSync scans on the source and destination.
question: How is using a manifest file different from using include filters?

values.display: CSV-formatted file

evidence.quote: A manifest is a CSV-formatted file that lists the file paths or object keys that should be included when the task runs and limits the scope of what is scanned by DataSync on the source and destination.

claim: DataSync task scheduling runs tasks automatically on the schedule you configure, with hourly, daily, or weekly options provided directly in the console.
question: Can I configure AWS DataSync to transfer on a schedule?

values.display: hourly, daily, or weekly options

qualifiers.scope: AWS DataSync task scheduling in the console

evidence.quote: Task scheduling automatically runs tasks on the schedule you configure, with hourly, daily, or weekly options provided directly in the Console.

claim: If a DataSync task is interrupted, for example by a network failure or an agent restart, the next run transfers the missing files and the data is complete and consistent at the end of that run, because each run is an incremental copy of the changes.
question: What happens if an AWS DataSync task is interrupted?

values.display: the next run of the task will transfer missing files

evidence.quote: If a task is interrupted, for instance, if the network connection goes down or the AWS DataSync agent is restarted, the next run of the task will transfer missing files, and the data will be complete and consistent at the end of this run. Each time a task is started it performs an incremental copy, transferring only the changes from the source to the destination.

claim: You can limit the network bandwidth a DataSync task uses with the built-in bandwidth throttle, and you can increase or decrease the limit while the task is running.
question: Can I control the amount of network bandwidth that an AWS DataSync task uses?

values.display: built-in bandwidth throttle

qualifiers.condition: limit can be changed while the task runs

evidence.quote: Yes. You can control the amount of network bandwidth that AWS DataSync will use by configuring the built-in bandwidth throttle. You can increase or decrease this limit while your data transfer task is running.

claim: You can use DataSync with your Direct Connect link to reach public service endpoints or private VPC endpoints; with VPC endpoints the data between the agent and AWS services does not traverse the public internet or need public IP addresses.
question: Can I use AWS DataSync with AWS Direct Connect?

values.display: public service endpoints or private VPC endpoints

qualifiers.scope: AWS DataSync agent to AWS services over Direct Connect
qualifiers.condition: VPC endpoints keep traffic off the public internet

evidence.quote: You can use AWS DataSync with your Direct Connect link to access public service endpoints or private VPC endpoints. When using VPC endpoints, data transferred between the DataSync agent and AWS services does not traverse the public internet or need public IP addresses, increasing the security of data as it is copied over the network.

claim: When copying data to or from your premises, DataSync needs no VPN or tunnel and no inbound connections, and the agent can route through a firewall using standard network ports.
question: Does AWS DataSync require setting up a VPN to connect to my destination storage?

values.display: no need to setup a VPN/tunnel or allow inbound connections

qualifiers.scope: AWS DataSync agent, on-premises to AWS

evidence.quote: No. When copying data to or from your premises, there is no need to setup a VPN/tunnel or allow inbound connections. Your AWS DataSync agent can be configured to route through a firewall using standard network ports.

claim: DataSync supports VPC endpoints, powered by AWS PrivateLink, for data movement, so transfers between the agent (on premises or in cloud) and AWS do not traverse the public internet or need public IP addresses.
question: Does AWS DataSync support VPC endpoints using AWS PrivateLink?

values.display: VPC endpoints are supported for data movement use cases

evidence.quote: Yes, VPC endpoints are supported for data movement use cases. You can use VPC endpoints to ensure data transferred between your AWS DataSync agent, either deployed on-premises or in-cloud, doesn't traverse the public internet or need public IP addresses.

claim: For data transfer between on premises and AWS storage services, a single DataSync task is capable of fully utilizing a 10 Gbps network link.
question: How fast can AWS DataSync copy my file system to AWS?

values.display: 10 Gbps network link

qualifiers.scope: one DataSync task, on premises to AWS storage
qualifiers.condition: actual speed also depends on source and destination I/O and network conditions

evidence.quote: For data transfer between on premises and AWS Storage services, a single DataSync task is capable of fully utilizing a 10 Gbps network link.
